**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics, Paper 3 (0765/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A lorry of mass $1400\ \mathrm{kg}$ moving along a straight horizontal road at a steady speed of $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ with its engine working at the rate of $96\ \mathrm{kW}$ experiences a constant non-gravitational resistance $R$.

(Take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.)
incertitudes: Question 4 (c) : « decreased by 20 kW » est lu comme une baisse de 20 kW par rapport à la puissance trouvée en (b), soit 40,8 - 20 = 20,8 kW, à la vitesse instantanée de 12 m s^-1 (une baisse à partir de 96 kW donnerait une accélération, non un retard, ce qui contredit « retardation »). Le sujet imprime « Take g as 10 m s^-2 » : valeur retenue g = 10.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Along the horizontal road the lorry is acted on by the driving force $F$ of the engine (forward) and the resistance $R$ (backward); the vertical forces (weight and normal reaction) cancel. Take the direction of motion as positive.

At a steady speed the acceleration is zero, so $F - R = 0$, i.e. $F = R$. The power of the engine is $P = Fv$:

$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{96\,000}{20} = 4800\ \mathrm{N}$$

**$R = 4800\ \mathrm{N}$.**
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: The lorry descends a plane inclined at $\sin^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac{1}{10}\right)$ to the horizontal with a steady speed of $12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Given that the non-gravitational resistance remains unchanged ($R = 4800\ \mathrm{N}$ from part (a)), calculate the rate at which the engine is now working.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Let $\theta$ be the angle of the slope, $\sin\theta = \tfrac1{10}$. Take the direction down the slope (the direction of motion) as positive. Forces along the slope: the driving force $F$ down the slope, the component of weight $mg\sin\theta$ down the slope, and the resistance $R$ up the slope.

$$mg\sin\theta = 1400\times 10\times\tfrac{1}{10} = 1400\ \mathrm{N}$$

Steady speed means zero acceleration:

$$F + mg\sin\theta - R = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; F = 4800 - 1400 = 3400\ \mathrm{N}$$

Rate of working of the engine:

$$P = Fv = 3400\times 12 = 40\,800\ \mathrm{W}$$

**The engine works at $40\,800\ \mathrm{W} = 40.8\ \mathrm{kW}$.**
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: The lorry descends the same plane (inclined at $\sin^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac{1}{10}\right)$ to the horizontal) at $12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ with the non-gravitational resistance still $R = 4800\ \mathrm{N}$ and the engine working at $40.8\ \mathrm{kW}$ as in part (b). Find the retardation of the lorry if the rate of working of the engine is decreased by $20\ \mathrm{kW}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**New power:** $40.8 - 20 = 20.8\ \mathrm{kW} = 20\,800\ \mathrm{W}$. At the instant when the power is reduced the speed is still $12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, so the new driving force is

$$F' = \frac{P'}{v} = \frac{20\,800}{12} = \frac{5200}{3}\ \mathrm{N} \approx 1733\ \mathrm{N}$$

**Equation of motion** down the slope (positive direction), with acceleration $a$:

$$F' + mg\sin\theta - R = ma$$

$$\frac{5200}{3} + 1400 - 4800 = 1400\,a \;\Rightarrow\; -\frac{5000}{3} = 1400\,a \;\Rightarrow\; a = -\frac{25}{21} \approx -1.19\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

The acceleration is negative (up the slope), so the lorry is slowing down.

**Retardation $= \tfrac{25}{21} \approx 1.19\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.**
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance
